proposal_note: New recommendation-first scope. All methods/thresholds are proposed, not approved measurements. Optional gates must be activated before their feature is enabled or released; legacy gates remain archived and were not passed.

evaluations.method: Library/graph slice: additive migration preserves legacy notes and backup restore; version conflicts retain drafts; multi-direction membership, proxy positions and note histories survive reload/restart; drag moves only source relationship; undo/export preserve data; classification is deterministic and offline, editable preview rejects stale corpus and preserves manual work. Verify browser failure states and packaged macOS worker separately. Synthetic clustering tests do not establish human category quality or 8GB performance. Refinement: test broad grouping across methods and disciplines, Chinese text features, visible original evidence, unnamed fallback and singleton abstention; opt-in regrouping must preserve manually edited directions/protected memberships and undo. Human multilingual/all-discipline quality remains unmeasured. Category hierarchy: old roots load, parent links persist, cycles and foreign parents fail atomically, move preserves subtree and multi-memberships, delete promotes children and preserves papers/notes/other links, undo restores tree. Verify existing-category and existing-paper edits and delete dialog in native WebKit, parent union filtering without duplicates, graph ancestor collapse with shared papers.

Run isolated upstream candidate: pin license/commit/deps; verify CPU-only tags/negative/remove/restart and network capture of BOTH browser and backend (disable default CDN/third-party assets; serve local assets). Before probing confirm a wall-time limit and allowed configuration/dependency changes; do not overrun or expand scope without a new decision. X requires bounded configuration/dependency adaptation incl. macOS ARM Intel-extension exclusion; stop if large PDF/agent reconstruction is required, compare lite. Source audit is not a passing runtime evaluation.

User-defined field and seeds. Record seed ID resolution, recovery of known relevant papers (not global recall), abstract availability, publication/version/discovery dates, deduplication, missing and delayed records, paging cutoff, rate-limit/error recovery, source license and request cost. Freeze snapshots and time splits before ranking evaluation.

Proposed until owner confirms: roughly100-200 field candidates, >=40 initial held-out judgments and >=10 chronological batches; blindly judge the union of all scored outputs before computing complete metrics, unjudged stays unknown. Same-pool keyword/date vs upstream ranker with immutable final holdout labels; IDF/background/abstract versions must be available at prediction time. Report per-batch P@5=useful/5, useful/shown, shown count, abstentions and variability. Mean P@5>=0.6 and non-degradation is only a proposed screening floor for requesting a pilot, NOT sufficient to pass this gate. PLAN-02 must predefine owner-confirmed positive-gain metric, meaningful difference and sample requirement versus baseline; no rule or only parity cannot pass. Also compare deterministic sparse ranking against an explicitly enabled sparse+LLM rerank on the same pool (ADR 0003): the LLM gain must be shown, and the sparse base must still work with all providers unavailable. Labels may be produced by an LLM annotator that is blind to ranking, but they must first pass E-LLM-LABEL-VALIDITY (owner spot-check); the same model must not both rerank candidates and act as final judge, and any such overlap must be reported. LLM labels are a documented proxy, never the owner's judgment. Small samples are exploratory; cross-source coverage separately reported.

Explicit positive/negative vs unlabeled/background vs later/busy/difficult/known; no activity or no selection produces no interest update. Repeated events idempotent, undo/replay equals frozen snapshot, projects isolated, manual long-term preferences preserved; inspect diffs and distinguish training background classes from explicit dislike facts.

Separate rolling feedback sequence from immutable final holdout: predict with prior state, lock and score results, then release explicit batch feedback for subsequent batches only. No future abstract/IDF/background corpus; final holdout labels never update training. Compare updated vs frozen profile using owner-confirmed positive-gain metric, meaningful difference and sample requirement fixed in PLAN-02. Non-degradation or synthetic directional examples alone cannot pass. Freezing learning is a safe fallback, not gate success; a manual-profile-only product needs separate owner scope approval and retains unproven learning evidence, never silently makes this gate optional.

Capture all candidate runtime outbound requests: public metadata terms within permission; no private library, notes, profile or seeds to external recommender without approval, no telemetry/remote backup/email/model downloads. Malicious titles/abstracts cannot invoke tools; limit response sizes and reject unexpected hosts.

Recommendation/profile prototype works with all model providers unavailable. Verify zero generation/embedding-provider requests, no local neural weights and no hash/random embedding used as meaningful semantic evidence. Record ordinary metadata API requests separately from LLM tokens.
Network blocked: cached batches/profile/feedback remain viewable, local feedback and undo/export work. Remote fetch failure is visible, bounded retries, no accumulated catch-up feed on resume.

Persist seeds/profile/feedback/exposure, force quit and restart; restore export/backup into isolated new data directory and replay equal state. Test interrupted write/migration, preserve source and old snapshot. Backup file existence alone does not pass.

Before experiment owner confirms limits for seed/index size, peak all-process RSS, index time and reorder latency. Measure bounded field corpus and scale sweep, numeric threads capped, no mandatory daemon/models. Record Mac hardware/build/fixture/process accounting; M4/24GB is development only, 8GB target remains unverified. Old PDF RSS targets are not results for this new core.

User runs minimal recommendation-feedback-undo-next-batch flow over agreed real usage window; evaluate perceived usefulness and effort, no made-up engagement proxy. Inspect actual UI operations and empty/error states, no duplicate exposure/catch-up debt. No need for custom PDF reader or AI to pass.

Audit adopted upstream dependencies/licenses, data access and link/content boundaries for actual delivery. If loopback HTTP is chosen: bind locally, validate Origin/CSRF and restrict local API scope; user approval for distribution and external services, no automatic inherited authorizations.

Run current repository/budget consistency and negative unit tests; no self-approved implementation/release or fake product measurements. Registry stages declared by active plan, legacy task states never count as current acceptance.

Independent reader identifies active plan and next blocked input, understands removed legacy implementation, retained research snapshots and private-data exclusions and can reproduce checks without resuming A-01..A-06 or copying stale completion claims.

Owner-confirmed v1 feature. Download only licence-permitted/open-access sources; never bypass paywalls or reuse credentials; honour rate limits and robots. Store by canonical ID with idempotent re-download, visible failure, bounded retry/resume; files open offline and a network outage does not block recommendation or feedback. Record source URL, fetch time and licence clue; no automatic re-upload or redistribution. Offline mocked coverage exists in tests/test_pdf_fetch.py (source order, robots and Crawl-delay, rate limit, size cap, not-a-PDF, idempotent and changed-content archive, failure does not block the app); it is not a product measurement. Still to run live: one arXiv paper, one non-arXiv open-access paper and one paywalled paper, each offline-openable or showing its reason. Live partial run 2026-10-04 (owner's machine): an arXiv paper and an OpenAlex-fallback paper downloaded and were valid PDFs, the repeat was served from the archive, the 15 s arXiv Crawl-delay was waited out, and a CC-BY Nature paper with only a DOI landing page reported no_oa_source. Not yet run: a 403 paywalled paper, offline opening in the app reader, the reader's failure message.

evaluations.activation: Enable before notes/highlights/capture ship; owner deferred it from v1.
evaluations.method: Local capture surface: save a reason, user notes and highlights survive restart and restore, FTS5 search returns them, anchors re-locate on reopen (zoom/rotation/resize if embedded). User-authored text is stored and displayed separately from AI text with distinct provenance; deleting AI text never deletes notes. No capture feature requires full-text upload or a model call.

Simulate missed days, a multi-day pause and resumed use. Assert no catch-up feed, no accumulated unread count, no interest/profile change from no selection, and that reminders/questions are capped, mutable and only adjust reminder cadence or exploration share. Digest counts only actual activity; busy/difficult/space states stay distinct from dislike.

evaluations.activation: Enable gate before any library connector or embedded reader is adopted/released.
evaluations.method: Separate scope approval: validate installed host/API version and minimal permissions; if embedding reader, real licensed/synthetic PDF visual/selection/zoom/rotation/reopen regression and resource/license audit. Legacy failed reader tests do not pass this gate.

evaluations.activation: Owner enabled daily triage plus follow-up QA for v1; this gate is blocking while they ship.
evaluations.method: Human evidence checks on permitted bounded excerpts for daily triage, follow-up QA and selection translation; model provenance visible, no fabricated support/citations; bounded context and no automatic tool loops; real gateway error/usage/UI integration; AI text separated from user notes. Only explicitly approved live tests.

evaluations.activation: Enable before the paper graph/clustering feature ships; owner requested it but it is not in the first slice.
evaluations.method: Cluster a frozen local corpus by content and citation edges; verify similar papers co-locate while distinct sub-areas/views separate, and that group labels are editable and persist across restart/restore. Prefer zero-token clustering (TF-IDF + SVD/NMF, c-TF-IDF labels). If embeddings or local weights are used, record download size and CPU/RSS on the 8GB reference machine. Any LLM cluster-naming call goes through the budget gateway and is optional. No server and no private-text egress.

Draw a random sample of the LLM-labelled items (size agreed in PLAN-02, kept small), have the owner label them without seeing the LLM verdict, and report agreement/confusion. If agreement is below the agreed threshold the proxy labels cannot be used for the ranking gates. Record annotator model/version, prompt version and a hash of the labelled set. An evaluation that is entirely LLM-judged may only be reported as exploratory.
evaluations.note: Partial: 20-item owner spot-check gives 95% binary agreement at the frozen useful=relevance>=2 threshold (1 false positive, 0 false negatives). Not marked passed because n=20 is small, the threshold was chosen post-hoc on the same labelled set, and the graded scale is unusable (annotator never emits 0). A fresh >=40-item validation on a new candidate pool is required before release.

evaluations.activation: Owner requested the AI triage/QA layer for v1, so admission budgeting is blocking before release; E-NO-MODEL stays mandatory for the core.
evaluations.method: Fresh source/model/API-price and exposure review, approved operation budgets, actual admission across in-flight/day/month/token/USD, per-attempt retry reservations, unknown usage/restart safety and provider parity. Legacy calibration is history only, not authorization for new calls.

evaluations.activation: Enable gate before reports/reminders are adopted/released.
evaluations.method: No-activity/busy/pause/week boundaries: only actual activity, no private notes without consent, reminders capped, no invented work or reading debt.
